title: Do Deterministic Verifiers Reduce Unsafe LLM-Generated Network Changes? A Paired Shared-Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment evaluating whether coupling a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) with a deterministic NetOps verifier+gate (generate→validate→repair, single automated repair attempt, shared_initial_candidate semantics) reduces unsafe intent-to-configuration proposals relative to the same initial LLM candidate observed without gating. Using a fixed deterministic task index (n=200 paired intents) drawn from a synthetic intent corpus and a Batfish‑style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) in a sandbox, every paired episode produced a valid configuration under both baseline (LLM-alone) and guarded conditions (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered confirmatory estimand (paired difference in unsafe-proposal rate) was 0.0 (exact two-sided p=1.0). Exploratory diagnostics show no automated repairs were applied and median latencies were dominated by shared initial generation. We report the full preregistered design, execution manifest, and analysis. Interpretation: under the selected synthetic tasks, model, and strict shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded validator pipeline did not change outcomes because the initial candidates were already valid; this null result neither proves universal equivalence nor contradicts prior work showing validators can reduce hallucinations in other settings. We discuss construct, internal, external, and conclusion-validity limitations and outline next-step experiments (higher baseline unsafe-rate tasks, multi-model evaluation, validator-only arm, real emulation).

sections.introduction: Motivation: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks (intent-to-configuration translation, runbook generation, limited self-healing). Prior surveys and empirical work emphasize that operational reliability depends heavily on system-level guardrails—retrieval, validators, and assurance contracts—rather than the model alone [1],[2],[3]. Research gap: there is limited published, reproducible paired evidence comparing an identical LLM initial candidate observed without gating versus that same candidate after a deterministic verifier+gate (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Research question (confirmatory): Compared to LLM-alone generation, does coupling the LLM with a deterministic verifier and deterministic accept/reject gate (with a single bounded automated repair attempt) reduce unsafe network-change proposals on a fixed paired intent set? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired design and frozen execution; (2) an autonomous run (n=200 paired intents) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic Batfish-style validator; (3) confirmatory and exploratory analyses and an evidence-grounded discussion of implications and limitations.
sections.related_work: LLM use in NetOps and AIOps has rapidly expanded with work on intent-based translation, runbook generation, and agentic NetOps; surveys highlight hallucination risks and the centrality of surrounding machinery (RAG, validators, contracts) for operational trustworthiness [1],[2],[3]. Deterministic validators and generate–validate–repair architectures are advocated in NetOps and adjacent domains (software repair, safety-critical agents) as practical paths to safer automation [4],[5]. Empirical studies in AIOps and DevOps show retrieval+checkers reduce unsafe command emissions but do not guarantee zero hallucination [6]. Threat models (poisoning, adversarial data) and benchmarking gaps (lack of validator-coupled NetOps benchmarks) motivate controlled paired experiments that preserve construct validity [7],[8].
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The experiment (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) preregistered the confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Key design choices (frozen before execution): model=gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses), execution_mode=scientific_confirmatory, generation semantics=shared_initial_candidate (one initial candidate shared across paired conditions), task_count=200 paired intents, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1, deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator+deterministic gate), adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Sampling and tasks: 200 intents selected deterministically from a synthetic intent generator (intent families: VLAN migrations, failover workflows, MTU upgrades) with difficulty labels; selection fixed prior to model calls. Primary metric: binary unsafe_flag (any reachability or policy violation reported by the validator). Analysis plan: paired binary test (McNemar-equivalent via registered paired_binary_analysis_v1), two-sided alpha=0.05; failed-call policy: complete_pair_primary. Execution provenance: full execution manifest, artifact hashes, and initial-master-prompt reference recorded (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 provided in Disclosure). Shared_initial_candidate semantics and the preregistered contract imply the baseline single-shot outcome equals the initial candidate; only the validator/repair/gate (in guarded arm) may alter the final accepted configuration. Implementation details: runs were sandboxed; no live device changes. All raw responses, validator traces, and repair logs archived.
sections.results: Execution summary: planned episodes=400 (200 pairs), completed episodes=400, failed episodes=0, model_calls_used=200 (shared-initial generation per pair). Confirmatory outcome (predeclared): complete_pair_count=200; contingency table: n11=200 (both safe), n10=0 (guarded safe only), n01=0 (baseline safe only), n00=0 (both unsafe). Paired difference (guarded minus baseline) = 0.0; exact two-sided p=1.0; 95% paired-bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]. Secondary/ exploratory observations: no automated repair was applied in any guarded episode (repair_applied=false for all guarded traces), validator reported valid=true for all final configurations. Latency: median end-to-end latency dominated by shared initial generation; guarded path added negligible extra time because no repair attempts were invoked. Representative per-task artifacts and validator traces are archived (examples in manuscript evidence bundle).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: Under the preregistered settings (single model, shared_initial_candidate, synthetic task generator, deterministic validator, single repair attempt), the guarded verifier pipeline did not change outcomes because the shared initial candidates generated by gpt-5-mini were valid for all sampled intents. This result is a valid confirmatory null for the preregistered estimand in this experimental context; it does not imply that validators are unnecessary in general. Possible contributing factors: (a) synthetic tasks and generator seed produced intents with high baseline solvability; (b) shared_initial_candidate semantics mean no independent guarded-first generation was executed—guarding could only accept/reject/repair the same candidate; (c) a single strong LLM and conservative prompt settings may have produced high-quality initial outputs; (d) the validator's coverage and the task specification aligned with reference answers. Relation to prior work: prior studies showing reduced hallucination with retrieval or checkers typically evaluate pipelines where the guarded condition either (i) augments generation (RAG) or (ii) allows independent guarded generation; under shared_initial_candidate the measurable effect is limited to validator-caused accept/reject/repair outcomes. Operational implication: experimental detection of verifier benefits requires task banks with nontrivial baseline unsafe rates or a different execution semantics (e.g., independent conditioned generation for guarded arm). Recommendations: future paired studies should (1) include tasks designed to produce a measurable baseline unsafe rate (e.g., adversarial or out-of-distribution intents), (2) evaluate an explicit validator-only arm and an independent guarded-generation arm, (3) test multiple LLMs and temperature/settings, (4) evaluate in richer emulation environments (live sandboxes) and with human-in-the-loop approval workflows.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment comparing an LLM-alone single-shot outcome versus that same initial candidate after a deterministic verifier+gate with bounded automated repair. In this run (n=200 paired intents, gpt-5-mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, shared_initial_candidate semantics) every initial candidate was valid and the guarded verifier did not change any outcomes; the preregistered paired difference was 0.0. This null finding is evidence about the executed estimand and execution context only. It highlights the necessity of careful construct design (task selection and generation semantics) for measurable evaluation of verifier benefits. We provide the archived artifacts, analysis, and a roadmap for follow-up experiments that target settings with nontrivial baseline unsafe rates, multiple models, independent guarded generation arms, and realistic emulation to better characterize when and how deterministic validators improve operational safety.

limitations: Internal validity: the study used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial LLM candidate per paired unit). Because baseline and guarded outcomes begin from the same candidate, any difference can only arise from the validator/repair; the design therefore cannot measure effects of guarded-conditioned regeneration.

Construct validity: tasks were synthetic and deterministically selected; the binary unsafe_flag (validator-detected reachability/policy violations) depends on the validator's coverage and rules and may not capture all operationally relevant risks (e.g., transient performance regressions or vendor-specific side effects outside validator rules).

External validity: single LLM (gpt-5-mini), single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions.

Conclusion validity: the observed null effect (paired difference = 0) reflects this execution's sampling frame where baseline generation produced only valid candidates; the study was powered to detect ~10 percentage-point reductions but cannot rule out smaller effects in other contexts.

Operational relevance: no live device changes were executed (sandboxed validation only); operational benefits (reduced triage time, deployment safety) were not measured and remain hypotheses for future field studies.
Security/contamination: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; the experiment did not evaluate retrieval-based poisoning vectors (no RAG was used).
